title: SDK client evolution: unified pagination, retry, and streaming migration PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level PRD to standardize how Redwood SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement pagination, retries, and streaming with a migration path that preserves customer contracts and enables new streaming resume semantics. The goal is to deliver a single developer experience across languages while minimizing breaking changes and offering clear migration steps.
background: Multiple SDK implementations diverged over the last two years. Differences: cursor token naming and encoding (base64 vs JSON), retry defaults and idempotency handling, and streaming resume behavior (some clients reconnect and re-request ranges while others rely on ephemeral session state). Customers using long-running streams and large result sets have seen inconsistent resume semantics and ambiguous migration pain during server-side model variant rollouts.
goals: 1) Define a canonical pagination contract (cursor-first, opaque token, stable across model rollouts). 2) Specify retry semantics and default backoff for safe idempotent retries. 3) Standardize streaming APIs including resume tokens and reconnection behavior. 4) Provide language-specific adapter guidance and a clear migration guide to avoid breaking client applications.
non_goals: We will not change server-side behavior for existing endpoints beyond adding optional headers/fields needed for resume/compatibility. We are not reworking billing or telemetry surfaces in this ticket.
requirements: R1: Pagination must support opaque cursor tokens with server-supplied 'cursor' and client-passback 'cursor' semantics. Token encoding must be versioned (v1 prefix) to allow future schema changes.
R2: APIs must expose deterministic 'page_size' and 'next_cursor' fields. Default page_size = 100, max page_size = 1000 unless endpoint-specific override.
R3: Retries: define idempotency policy per endpoint. Read-only/list endpoints are safe to retry. Mutating endpoints must require an idempotency-key header to be retried by client SDKs.
R4: Backoff policy: default exponential backoff with full jitter, base = 200ms, cap = 5s, max attempts = 5 for transient network/5xx errors and 429 throttling.

R5: Streaming APIs must provide resume semantics using 'resume_token' emitted frequently in the stream (every N messages or every T seconds). Resume tokens must be stable across small server restarts and model rollouts where possible.

R6: SDKs must provide first-class helpers: Paginator abstraction with async and sync iterators, retry policy object, streaming client with auto-reconnect+resume and hooks for application-level checkpointing.
R7: Compatibility: New SDK versions must be backward compatible for 2 major releases (semver) and provide opt-in preview flags for new behavior.
R8: Observability hooks: SDKs must emit structured events for 'retry', 'resume_attempt', 'resume_success', and 'pagination_boundary' to telemetry when enabled.
R9: Migration: Provide a toggle flag 'use_new_pagination' in SDKs to allow staged rollouts for customers.
R10: Test coverage: End-to-end integrations including resume scenarios with simulated partial writes, and chaos tests that kill server connections mid-stream.
api_examples: Notes: examples above use a common pattern: SDK exposes a Paginator abstraction that can be 'for' or 'for await' style depending on language, and a streaming client that emits a 'resume_token' field occasionally. Resume tokens are opaque strings that start with 'rwd_v1:' to allow server parsing.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: All three language SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement the Paginator abstraction with documented examples and pass the pagination integration test matrix (forward/backward paginated iteration, page size limits, empty results).
AC2: Retry module present in each SDK with configurable policy; default policy matches R4 and unit tests validate retry/backoff sequence and max attempts.
AC3: Streaming client exposes resume_token and auto-resume behavior behind a feature flag; resume unit/integration tests cover reconnect + resume success and resume failure fallbacks.
AC4: Migration toggle 'use_new_pagination' implemented in SDKs and documented in migration guide; enabling toggle on legacy clients must not break existing server contracts.
AC5: No breaking changes to existing public surface by default; any breaking change must be behind explicitly opt-in preview flag and documented in the release notes.
AC6: Observability events emitted match schema and appear in staging telemetry dashboards during validation runs.
AC7: Performance guardrails: Paginator and streaming path must not regress median latency by more than 15% in bench tests vs current baseline for typical page sizes.
AC8: Documentation: PRD-linked migration guide, code samples, and compatibility matrix published to the SDK docs site before stable release.
AC9: Security review completed for idempotency-key and resume_token handling (no PII in tokens).
compatibility_matrix: Server v1 (current): supports opaque cursors and streaming without resume_token. New SDKs must be compatible and fall back to non-resumable streams when interacting with older server nodes.
Server v1.1 (rolling rollout): emits resume_token header 'x-rwd-resume' and supports resume endpoints. SDKs enable resume when 'x-rwd-resume' is present.
SDK behavior: default = backward compatible. New behavior behind 'use_new_pagination' or 'enable_stream_resume' toggles. Expect to maintain compatibility for 2 major SDK releases.
Cursor token format: 'rwd_v1:<base64-json>'. Older clients that believe token is raw base64 must be handled by server-side dual-parse for one release window.
Idempotency: If client supplies 'idempotency-key', server will dedupe for 24 hours. New SDKs will add an opt-in auto-idempotency helper for retrying mutating calls.
Deprecation policy: Any contract removed will have a 6-month deprecation window and tooling guidance to migrate.

Edge cases: If resume_token refers to an evicted cache window, server returns 410 with a suggested fallback cursor; SDKs must surface this to the application and provide transparent fallbacks (restart from suggested cursor).
migration_strategy: 1) Launch alpha SDKs behind preview flags with 'use_new_pagination' and 'enable_stream_resume' for early adopters. Collect feedback for 3 weeks.
2) Run compatibility lab: replay recorded production traces against SDKs+server v1.1 in staging, verify resume success rate >= 99% and pagination parity.
3) Publish migration guide with code diffs for Python/TS/Go and script to bulk-convert stored cursor tokens when feasible.
4) Gradual rollout: opt-in customers -> beta customers via feature gates -> default stable release after 8 weeks and telemetry confirmation.
5) Post-release: deprecate old toggle after 2 major releases with migration automation and warnings in SDK logs when old cursor formats are detected.
6) Provide a backfill job template for customers who stored legacy cursors where we can offer a 'cursor-migrate' endpoint in limited cases.
rollback_plan: If a critical regression is discovered (resume failure rate > 1% or pagination parity failure impacting correctness), revert client-side toggle by shipping a patch that disables 'use_new_pagination' and coordinate with server to temporarily disable resume headers. For severe server regressions, roll server change back and notify impacted customers with mitigation steps.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for Paginator and RetryPolicy in each SDK with >90% coverage for the module.
Integration tests: staging harness that runs the SDK against a server matrix (v1, v1.1, canary) including simulated network partitions, 429 spikes, and mid-stream connection kills.
Performance tests: microbench comparing median token latency and tail latency for streaming and pagination paths; ensure <15% regression.
Chaos tests: orchestrate random TCP connection drops and verify auto-resume behavior and telemetry events.
Security/PII checks: automated scans to confirm resume_token and cursor payloads do not include raw user content or secrets.
Compatibility tests: parse-layer validator that accepts both legacy and new cursor formats for one release window.
decisions: D1: Use opaque, server-supplied cursor tokens (rwd_v1) rather than exposing internal offsets; reason: future-proofing and multi-model sharding compatibility.
D2: Default retry policy will use exponential backoff with full jitter, 5 attempts; reason: balance between transient recoverability and latency predictability.
D3: Streaming resume is opt-in behind flags and enabled automatically if server advertises 'x-rwd-resume'; reason: avoid breaking older server nodes and allow staged rollouts.
D4: SDKs will not attempt to synthesize resume tokens; tokens are authoritative from server only.
D5: Provide explicit opt-in auto-idempotency helpers for client libraries to retry mutating calls safely when developers opt in.
